articles.title: Urgent Care Radiography for Low Back Pain Is Rarely Followed by Emergency Advanced Imaging.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Workup of low back pain (LBP) in emergency departments (EDs) commonly involves CT or MRI, even though guidelines reserve advanced imaging for patients with red flags. We measured how often urgent care center (UCC) radiography for low-acuity LBP was followed by advanced imaging in the ED within 30 days, and compared per-study resource intensity between UCC radiography and ED CT or MRI. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults imaged for LBP at 23 UCCs and affiliated EDs between 2019 and 2025. We excluded red-flag presentations by screening keywords from the order indication. We identified 30-day returns by linking medical record numbers between cohorts, and two radiologists reviewed each one. Resource intensity was measured as Total Relative Value Units (RVU) per study, converted to approximate Medicare-allowed dollars. RESULTS: Among 16,754 studies (2,924 UCC radiographs, 13,830 ED studies) from 15,759 patients, UCC patients were younger (median 50 vs 67 years, P < 0.001). Median Total RVU was 1.43 (UCC) versus 5.14 (ED) (about $48 vs $171, P < 0.001). Twenty-four UCC studies were followed by ED advanced imaging within 30 days (0.82%, 95% CI 0.55-1.22), 12 within 24 hours. Radiologists judged one return a true radiographic miss. Return rates were similar across UCC networks (P = 1.00). DISCUSSION: UCC radiography for low-acuity LBP was rarely followed by ED advanced imaging within 30 days and entailed lower per-study imaging resource use than ED CT or MRI.

articles.title: If Not Now, When? Follow-Up Imaging for Patients Who Are Incarcerated.
4DLoG: Generative modeling of neurodegenerative brain anatomy with 4D longitudinal diffusion model.
articles.abstract: Modeling and predicting neurodegenerative disease progression from medical images remains a major challenge in medical AI, with significant implications for early diagnosis, disease monitoring, and treatment planning. However, most longitudinal neuroimaging datasets are temporally sparse, with substantial gaps and missing follow-up scans for individual subjects. This makes it difficult to learn and accurately capture the continuous anatomical changes associated with disease progression at the level of individual subjects. To address this problem, we propose a novel model, named as 4DLoG, a full 4D (3D×T) Longitudinal Generative framework that effectively models and synthesizes follow-up brain anatomy over time, conditioned on available clinical and demographic variables. In contrast to previous approaches, our 4DLoG features two main contributions. First, it introduces a full 4D generative diffusion framework that jointly models spatial and temporal dependencies across complete longitudinal sequences through dedicated spatiotemporal attention, with robust spatial patch extraction and temporal alignment. Second, it explicitly learns the distribution of topology-preserving spatiotemporal deformations, which captures realistic geometric changes in brain structures over time. These new components enable a better generation of anatomically plausible future states from an imaging scan at any time point, providing greater flexibility for modeling individual longitudinal brain trajectories. We validate our model through both synthetic sequence generation and downstream longitudinal disease classification, as well as brain segmentation. Experiments on two large-scale longitudinal neuroimage datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in generating anatomically accurate, temporally consistent, and clinically meaningful brain trajectories. Our code is available on Github.

articles.title: Anatomy-informed CT Spatial Phenotype Associated with Extrapancreatic Perineural Invasion in Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable CT spatial phenotype associated with extrapancreatic perineural invasion (EPNI) in resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This multicenter study included training, internal testing, neoadjuvant testing, retrospective external testing, prospective external testing, and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) sets. The Preoperative Risk of Perineural High-risk Extension in Tumors (PROPHET) model and threshold were locked before testing. Performance was assessed with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and threshold metrics. Six radiologists compared unaided and assisted readings. A stratified Cox model related PROPHET risk to survival, adjusting for age, sex, tumor size, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, nodal category, and differentiation. Results Among 1854 patients (median age, 63 years; 1131 male), AUCs were 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.96) in prospective external testing, 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.93) in retrospective external testing, 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.95) after neoadjuvant therapy, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.98-> 0.99) in internal testing, and 0.80 (95% CI, 0.68-0.93) in TCIA. TCIA sensitivity and specificity were 24/30 (80%) and 2/19 (11%). Assistance increased mean sensitivity to 93% from 82% and reduced reading time to 3.02 from 3.64 minutes per patient (both Holm-adjusted P < .001). Higher PROPHET risk was associated with shorter survival (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.53-2.47; nominal P < .001). Conclusion PROPHET provides a CT-visible tumor-vessel spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license.

articles.title: Automation Bias and Deskilling in Radiology AI: A Confidence-stratified Triage Model for Workflow Integration.
articles.abstract: Radiology is adopting artificial intelligence (AI) faster than it is studying what AI does to radiologists' perceptual expertise and interpretive skill. The question has partly shifted from whether these tools perform well on benchmark tasks to what happens to clinical judgment when use of these tools becomes routine. Two risks accompany this transition: automation bias, the tendency to follow AI suggestions without adequate scrutiny, and deskilling, the erosion of perceptual and interpretive ability through disuse, typically revealed when AI support is withdrawn. Incorrect AI output degrades accuracy regardless of experience, the benefit of assistance varies unpredictably across readers and tasks, and performance falls after AI withdrawal; neither risk has been studied longitudinally in radiology. A confidence-stratified triage model is proposed in which calibrated AI confidence, not findings alone, routes cases to low-, intermediate-, or high-confidence streams: output withheld until independent reading, shown with uncertainty signals and a checklist, or shown with random blinded audit. Demonstrated local confidence calibration is a precondition for deployment, and stream thresholds and audit rates should be weighted by task and potential clinical harm, not error probability alone. Rather than applying one workflow to every case, the model redistributes radiologist attention to where AI error is most likely and most consequential, operationalizing four principles: keeping the radiologist in the decision loop, making AI uncertainty visible, inserting targeted cognitive friction, and governing the human-AI interaction as a system. A research agenda to determine whether these countermeasures reduce automation bias and skill erosion in practice is also proposed.

articles.title: Reversal of Lumbar Spinal Epidural Lipomatosis in a Patient Using GLP-1 Agonist.
Navigating the Academic Enterprise as a Community Radiologist.
A Framework for Identifying and Understanding Cognitive Biases in Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Radiology.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) creates new susceptibility to diagnostic error in radiology related to the cognitive processes by which radiologists' interpretations incorporate AI outputs. This Perspective presents a conceptual framework for cognitive biases in AI-assisted radiology linking specific biases to radiologist-AI interactions. The framework uses dual-process theory, recognizing fast intuitive and deliberate analytic modes of information processing, as an organizing model for understanding cognitive processes underlying radiologists' decisions and their potential contribution to bias. Across seven decision scenarios spanning image viewing, findings interpretation, and contextual integration, the framework examines how AI output timing, radiologist-AI agreement, trust calibration, and reader expertise influence decision-making. We identify adaptive heuristics that support efficient decisions but, when misapplied or overrelied upon, increase susceptibility to complacency, confirmation, automation, distrust, anchoring, and usual implication bias, and increase behavioral risk of use without qualification. We highlight AI paradoxes emerging from the framework of despecialization, system fragility, and deskilling. Finally, we propose strategies targeting these cognitive biases, including education and experiential learning, workflow and interface design, clinical oversight, and performance monitoring. This framework provides a structured basis for generating testable hypotheses and designing AI-assisted radiology systems that preserve the strengths of human expertise and AI while supporting calibrated reliance.

The Role of Amide Proton Transfer Imaging in Brain Tumor Management.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Amide Proton Transfer Weighted (APTw) imaging is an emerging technique that provides crucial insights about tumor biology. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This narrative clinical review summarizes the physics and implementation of APTw imaging and critically evaluates its role in brain tumor management, with emphasis on adult diffuse gliomas. Relationship with other routine clinical sequences, aspects of standardization and reproducibility, key limitations, and future directions are also discussed. RESULTS AND CONCLUSION: Evidence supports potential value for tumor grading, biopsy targeting, molecular characterization, assessment of infiltrative tumor, and differentiation of tumor progression from treatment-related change. However, wider clinical translation will require harmonized acquisition and processing, cross-vendor validation, and prospective multicenter studies with standardized reference standards.

Spot size reduction and minibeam creation in a proton PBS nozzle using multipole permanent magnets.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Smaller spot sizes in pencil beam scanning (PBS) nozzles are generally desired to allow more conformal treatments and to spare normal tissue and organs at risk. The production of small diameter proton beams, especially proton minibeams, is challenging because long drift spaces in standard PBS nozzles exacerbate effects of MCS and finite beam divergence. PURPOSE: To investigate the use of multipole magnets in a proton PBS nozzle to create pencil beams of reduced spot size, including the creation of proton minibeams. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations were performed in a shortened He-filled nozzle incorporating a doublet of octupole magnets and a single quadrupole magnet modeled as Halbach cylinders. Beam diameter reduction was realized by the combination of octupole tail folding and quadrupole magnetic focusing. The octupole doublet was positioned at nozzle entrance upstream of the scanning magnets and the quadrupole was (optionally) positioned at the nozzle exit. The nozzle was configured for four modes of operation, roughly described as standard pencil beam (PB mode), reduced-diameter pencil beam (PBR), symmetric minibeam (MB), and planar minibeam (MBP). Depending on nozzle mode, symmetric beam spots were produced by a continuous rotation (i.e., spinning) of the octupole doublet and the quadrupole magnet about the beam axis. Particle energies investigated covered nearly the full range typically used in clinical applications (70, 100, 150, and 225 MeV). A symmetric Gaussian beam model was used with σ = 3 mm (FWHM = 7 mm) and σ' (divergence) chosen from literature. Pencil beam and reduced diameter pencil beam dose distributions in a water phantom were compared. Minibeam composite dose distributions were created by laterally shifting single beamlet distributions in one or two dimensions, and PVDR and beamlet FWHM were determined. Modulated beams in each nozzle mode were also created. RESULTS: FWHM, FW20M, and penumbra were reduced for all PBR pencil beams compared to unshaped PB beams: at nozzle exit FWHM and FW20M were 19%-38% lower and penumbra P80/20 were 14%-59% lower, and at Bragg depth the differential full widths and penumbra were generally present; with full widths up to 21% smaller, and penumbras up to 15% smaller. The creation of single-layer planar and symmetric minibeams in MBP and MB modes showed minimum beamlet FWHM near water phantom entrance (e.g., 10 mm WED) as low as 0.7-1.4 mm and <2 mm up to a range of 3-4.5 cm of the entrance channel. PVDR was the largest for MBP beams and was as high as 910, whereas PVDR for MB beams was as high as 144. Modulated PBR penumbra were smaller compared to similar PB beams. Modulated MB and MBP minibeams produced clinically relevant PVDR. That study results were achieved ∼1 m downstream of nozzle entrance and beyond is noteworthy. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed PBS nozzle could potentially be used to produce pencil beams and modulated beams with smaller spot sizes and penumbras, including proton minibeams, suitable for clinical or preclinical applications.

articles.title: Risk Stratification of Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS 3) Lesions in the Peripheral and Transition Zones Using Clinical and Quantitative MRI Markers.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) 3 lesions often undergo biopsy despite a low positive predictive value (< 25%) for clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa), defined as International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group ≥ 2. PURPOSE: To determine whether mean apparent diffusion coefficient (mADC), alone or with prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based metrics, improves zone-specific PI-RADS 3 classification for csPCa detection. STUDY TYPE: Retrospective, single-center. POPULATION: One hunderd and seventy-one males (71 ± 8 years) with 191 PI-RADS 3 lesions who underwent multiparametric MRI and targeted biopsy. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T, T2-weighted turbo spin-echo imaging, single-shot echo-planar diffusion-weighted imaging, and fat-suppressed dynamic contrast-enhanced T1-weighted gradient echo sequences. ASSESSMENT: mADC, PSA, PSA density (PSAD), prostate volume, and body mass index were analyzed. STATISTICAL TESTS: Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses assessed associations with malignancy and diagnostic performance. RESULTS: mADC was significantly lower in cancers than non-cancers in 133 PZ lesions (885 ± 165 vs. 1068 ± 168 × 10-6 mm2/s) and 58 TZ lesions (670 ± 127 vs. 832 ± 179 × 10-6 mm2/s). In the PZ, mADC alone, and with PSAD showed no significantly different area under the curve (AUC, 0.79 vs. 0.80, p = 0.28). A combination of mADC and PSAD would result in hypothetical estimated lesion-level biopsy avoidance. In the TZ, combining mADC with PSAD yielded significantly higher AUC than mADC alone (0.88 vs. 0.77, difference: 0.109 [95% CI: 0.010-0.208]). This combination would result in hypothetical estimated lesion-level biopsy avoidance in 58 of 82 non-cancers (71%) while missing one csPCa in the PZ, and 27 of 35 noncancerous lesions while missing one csPCa in TZ. DATA CONCLUSION: mADC combined with PSAD showed a significant increase in discrimination in the TZ, suggesting improved PI-RADS 3 stratification; independent validation is required before clinical implementation. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: 2.

articles.title: Patient reported swallowing outcomes after prophylactic versus reactive gastrostomy during chemoradiotherapy for head and neck cancer: Results from the SwallPEG randomized trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare prophylactic (p-) versus reactive (r-) percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement during definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for locally advanced, nonmetastatic head and neck carcinoma, with swallowing-related quality of life (QoL) as the primary endpoint. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SwallPEG is a prospective, multicenter, randomized phase III trial of patients undergoing definitive cisplatin-based CRT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to pPEG before CRT or rPEG based on predefined nutritional criteria. All received standardized nutritional counseling, weekly dietitian assessment, and swallowing rehabilitation. The primary endpoint was swallowing-related QoL at 6 months, assessed using the MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory (MDADI) composite score. Secondary endpoints included nutritional outcomes, treatment-related toxicity, PEG-related complications, and early oncologic outcomes. RESULTS: Fifty-seven patients were analyzed (pPEG, n = 28; rPEG, n = 29). Following a prespecified interim analysis that reached the futility boundary, the trial was closed early in the context of slow accrual. Median MDADI composite scores at 6 months were 69.5 (Q1-Q3, 60.0-80.0) and 74.7 (Q1-Q3, 58.9-87.9), respectively (P = 0.595). Swallowing function declined during CRT and subsequently recovered without a significant between-group difference. Weight loss at 6 months was comparable (-7.0 % vs - 9.0 %; P = 0.67). No significant differences were observed in treatment-related toxicity, PEG-related complications, chemotherapy delivery, or early oncologic outcomes. CONCLUSION: No difference in swallowing-related QoL was demonstrated between (p-) and rPEG strategies. Although interpretation is limited by early trial closure and reduced sample size, the findings support individualized PEG placement based on clinical need.

articles.title: A multimodal MRI study of DTI-ALPS and cerebral blood flow changes across the Alzheimer's disease continuum.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by cerebral blood flow (CBF) abnormalities and alterations in the neurofluid-related brain tissue environment, but their evolution along the AD continuum and links to cognitive decline and plasma biomarkers remain unclear. Using multimodal MRI, we quantified the diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index and CBF alterations and examined their associations with cognitive performance and plasma biomarkers across the AD continuum. METHODS: This study enrolled 78 healthy controls (HC), 53 subjective cognitive decline (SCD), 40 mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 110 AD. All subjects received MRI and neurocognitive assessments. The DTI-ALPS index was used as a diffusion-based marker of directional water diffusivity within periventricular white matter and the neurofluid-related tissue environment. CBF changes were calculated, and plasma biomarkers associated with neurodegeneration were measured. Partial correlation analysis explored relationships among ALPS index, CBF in cognition-related brain regions, cognitive scores, and plasma biomarkers. Statistical mediation analyses were performed to assess indirect effects involving the ALPS index and plasma biomarkers in the association between regional CBF and cognitive performance. RESULTS: ALPS index decreased stage-dependently along the AD continuum, significantly lower in MCI and AD versus HC and SCD. HC and SCD showed higher CBF than AD in right middle cingulate and left inferior parietal lobule. CBF in bilateral angular gyri and right superior frontal gyrus positively correlated with MoCA and RAVLT scores. Cognition-related CBF positively correlated with bilateral mean ALPS index, and negatively with NfL and p-tau217. Statistical mediation analyses identified significant indirect effects involving the bilateral mean ALPS index and plasma NfL in the association between regional CBF and cognitive performance. DISCUSSION: Cerebral hypoperfusion, altered DTI-ALPS measures, and axonal injury were closely associated across the AD continuum, suggesting interrelated neurovascular, neurofluid-related tissue, and neurodegenerative alterations associated with cognitive impairment.

articles.title: Impact of hearing loss on visual selective attention: Evidence from N2pc and resting-state networks.
articles.abstract: Efficient visual attention is fundamental to environmental adaptation and social interaction. While previous studies have observed alterations in visual processing among deaf individuals, findings remain controversial regarding whether these changes stem from hearing loss (sensory compensation vs. cognitive deficit) or sign language experience. To address this issue, the present study provides task-related and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) evidence to disentangle the specific drivers of visual selective attention plasticity. A visual search task was used to examine selective attention in 95 participants (34 prelingual deaf, 27 hearing signers, and 34 hearing nonsigners). Compared to both hearing groups, deaf individuals exhibited significantly lower hit rates and diminished N2-posterior contralateral (N2pc) amplitudes. Hearing signers and nonsigners showed comparable behavioral performance, N2pc amplitudes, and resting-state network topology, whereas the deaf group was further characterized by a degraded resting-state alpha network topology, evidenced by reduced clustering coefficients, global efficiency, and weakened frontal-occipital connectivity. N2pc amplitude correlated significantly with resting-state network properties and behavioral accuracy. These results suggest that deaf individuals may suffer from an imbalance in the regulation of visual selective attention, most clearly indexed by the evoked N2pc and by intrinsic alpha-network organization, and likely linked to increased resource competition following the loss of auditory monitoring. Our findings provide neurophysiological evidence that these attentional deficits are associated with hearing loss rather than with sign-language experience, offering a new perspective for understanding the boundaries of cross-modal plasticity in the human brain.

articles.title: Prospective evaluation of an optimized low-dose CT enterography protocol for patients with Crohn's disease.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate an optimized CT enterography (CTE) strategy combining reduced radiation exposure and iodine administration in patients with Crohn's disease (CD), with subjective image quality as the primary endpoint. METHODS: This prospective single-center randomized study enrolled 102 patients with CD who underwent CTE between February and October 2025. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio using a computer-generated random sequence, with allocation concealed in sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes opened by a research nurse not involved in patient enrollment, image evaluation, or clinical data collection. No stratification or blocking was used. The three protocols were: a standard-dose protocol (Group A), a low-dose protocol using 100 kVp and 70% adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction-V (ASIR-V) (Group B), and a combined low-dose, low-contrast protocol using the same acquisition settings with a reduced iodine dose (320 mgI/kg, corresponding to 1.0 mL/kg of contrast medium) (Group C). The primary endpoint was subjective image quality assessed using a 5-point Likert scale. Secondary endpoints included objective image quality, bowel wall enhancement, and radiation dose metrics. Diagnostic performance for disease activity and luminal stenosis was evaluated as an exploratory analysis in patients with an eligible endoscopic reference standard; the study was not designed or powered for diagnostic non-inferiority or equivalence testing. RESULTS: No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in baseline characteristics (all p > 0.05). For the primary endpoint, mean subjective image quality scores were 4.3 ± 0.5, 4.5 ± 0.6, and 4.5 ± 0.5 in Groups A, B, and C, respectively, with no significant between-group difference (p = 0.27); the between-group differences were 0.2 points (95% CI, -0.1 to 0.5) for Group B versus A, 0.2 points (95% CI, -0.1 to 0.5) for Group C versus A, and 0.0 points (95% CI, -0.3 to 0.3) for Group C versus B. Compared with the standard protocol, the estimated effective radiation dose was reduced by 53.2% in Group B and 50.0% in Group C (both p < 0.001), with no significant difference between the two optimized protocols. Both optimized protocols showed lower image noise and higher signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios than the standard protocol (all p < 0.05), whereas no statistically significant between-group differences were detected in bowel wall attenuation (all p > 0.05). For the exploratory diagnostic analysis, 76/102 patients had an eligible endoscopic reference standard (Group A, 25/31; Group B, 28/38; Group C, 23/33). Diagnostic accuracy for disease activity was 88.0% (95% CI, 70.0-95.8%) in Group A, 89.3% (95% CI, 72.8-96.3%) in Group B, and 87.0% (95% CI, 67.9-95.5%) in Group C; the corresponding between-group differences were 1.3 percentage points (95% CI, -16.8 to 19.4) for B versus A, -1.0 percentage points (95% CI, -19.4 to 17.4) for C versus A, and 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -16.6 to 21.2) for B versus C. For luminal stenosis, diagnostic accuracy was 84.0% (95% CI, 65.3-94.1%), 89.3% (95% CI, 72.8-96.3%), and 87.0% (95% CI, 67.9-95.5%), respectively; the absolute differences were 5.3 percentage points (95% CI, -12.1 to 22.7) for B versus A, 3.0 percentage points (95% CI, -15.2 to 21.2) for C versus A, and 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -16.6 to 21.2) for B versus C. The confidence intervals for between-group differences were wide and included values that could be clinically relevant; because the study was not powered to establish diagnostic non-inferiority or equivalence, the absence of statistically significant differences should not be interpreted as evidence of diagnostic equivalence or non-inferiority. CONCLUSION: On the GE Revolution 256-detector-row CT platform, the optimized CTE protocols reduced radiation exposure by approximately 50%, while Group C additionally achieved a protocol-defined 33.3% reduction in weight-normalized iodine dose. Based on the observed dose and image-quality findings, Group B can reasonably be recommended when radiation reduction is the primary goal, whereas Group C may be considered when both radiation and iodine reduction are desired. These findings do not establish equivalence or non-inferiority in image quality or diagnostic performance.

articles.title: Opportunistic screening of hip osteoporosis using Phantom-Less quantitative CT-Derived thoracic volumetric BMD from routine chest CT: A Multicentre, retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate diagnostic thresholds for thoracic volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) derived from routine chest CT scans, and to evaluate the performance of this metric for opportunistic screening of hip osteoporosis (hOP) and hip osteopenia in adults aged 60 years and older. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 568 patients aged 60 years and older who underwent both non-contrast chest computed tomography (CT) and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Thoracic quantitative CT-derived volumetric bone mineral density (Th-vBMD) was measured using a phantomless quantitative CT (PL-QCT) system. The robustness of the diagnostic model was evaluated through internal validation, including 500-iteration bootstrap resampling. The diagnostic performance of Th-vBMD was compared against the reference hip DXA T-score. RESULTS: A total of 568 patients were included. The prevalence of hOP and hip osteopenia was 36.3 % and 42.6 %, respectively. Th-vBMD demonstrated performance with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.873 (95 % CI: 0.837-0.910). The optimal Th-vBMD threshold for hOP was 85.4 mg/cm3, sensitivity 0.851 and specificity 0.864. The optimal threshold for hip osteopenia was 120.7 mg/cm3, sensitivity: 0.860 and specificity: 0.811. Logistic regression identified Th-vBMD ≤ 85.4 mg/cm3 as an independent predictor of hOP (adjusted OR: 26.70; 95 % CI: 16.3-45.0; p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This study establishes and validates Th-vBMD thresholds derived from routine chest CT for opportunistic hOP screening in elderly. This cost-effective strategy leverages clinical imaging data to identify individuals at osteoporosis risk, facilitating intervention and advancing osteoporosis prevention.

articles.title: Impact of reconstruction-based misalignment correction on image quality, reader agreement, and diagnostic confidence in single-source photon-counting CT.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Recently, a single-source photon-counting detector (PCD-CT) system with detector settings comparable to the dual-source system has been introduced. Although applicable to coronary CT angiography (CCTA), its lower temporal resolution may lead to more pronounced motion and misalignment artefacts. Image slab misalignment correction algorithm reduces these artefacts; therefore, we aimed to evaluate its effect on subjective image quality metrics on this PCD-CT system. METHODS: CCTA images were reconstructed with and without using misalignment correction algorithm. Four readers with varying experience evaluated coronary vessels using three image quality metrics: motion, misalignment artefact, and diagnostic confidence. Linear mixed-effect models were used to assess the effects of reconstruction type, image quality metrics, vessels, and readers. To assess reader agreement, intraclass correlation and multiple agreement metrics were used. RESULTS: 102 patients (53.9% female) were included in the final analysis. The type of reconstruction significantly affected image quality metric scores (p = 0.031). Post-hoc analysis showed that misalignment corrected reconstruction significantly improved misalignment artefacts (Δ = 0.94, 95% CI, 0.88-0.99, p < 0.01) and diagnostic confidence (Δ = 0.296, 95% CI, 0.24-0.36, p < 0.01). Misalignment correction showed a more modest effect on motion artefacts (Δ = 0.065, 95% CI, 0.008-0.122, p = 0.026). Inter-rater reliability was good for both reconstruction types (ICC = 0.713 and ICC = 0.657 for original dataset and corrected dataset). Agreement with the most experienced reader improved using misalignment correction (Exact agreement with the least experienced reader: 43.3% and 54.1%). CONCLUSION: The correction algorithm reduced misalignment artefacts and enhanced subjective diagnostic confidence on single-source PCD-CT, with benefits observed across readers of varying experience.

articles.title: Development and evaluation of X-ray lithophanes as test objects for interventional procedure simulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In the growing field of interventional radiology, emerging technologies implement the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help tackle growing demands for treatment. Due to the anatomical differences in animals, volunteers offer the most realistic training and testing scenario, however safety considerations restrict rapid prototyping of these new technologies. Simulators have been a key facilitator in the testing of new technologies among numerous medical engineering studies, but often lack the realism to reliably test AI. PURPOSE: This proof-of-concept study presents methods to create or enhance hyper-realistic radiographic simulators that can effectively function with a medical-grade AI software. METHODS: Iron-filled plastic was used to three-dimensionally (3D) print a series of blocks of heights up to 30 mm. By analyzing the intensities generated by different thicknesses of plastic, anonymous fluoroscopic images were turned into height maps (lithophanes) and 3D-printed. A static scene from transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was then 3D-printed and imaged with different presets using two different x-ray systems for mathematical analysis. Lithophanes were then used as a radiographic background to experimental and commercial interventional simulators to test Caranx Medical's TAVIPILOT AI. Finally, fluoroscopies from 5 3D-printed lithophanes were mixed with 5 real images and presented to 5 expert volunteers to establish their realism in a structured survey. RESULTS: The 3D-printed x-ray lithophanes test-plates' radiographic appearance was rated as "Adequate" to "Good" across all fields of the survey, with participants praising their realism. The test-plate was able to reliably recreate the TAVI scene in different x-ray systems, with joint-histogram correlation coefficients above 0.9, and global structural similarity above 0.8. The lithophanes were imaged as a standalone test plate and as a backing to dynamic TAVI interventional simulators; in both cases, TAVIPILOT AI responded to the simulator as if it was operating on a real anatomical image. CONCLUSIONS: Lithophane plates present an easy-to-implement solution to recreate monoplane x-ray scenes, which can be deployed to test software at the point of care with minimal logistical, ethical, or safety concerns. This study opens the door for a new range of interventional simulators able to recreate human-like appearance to test AI, offering a non-exclusive alternative to patient volunteers and anonymous data.

articles.title: Regularization in multiplexed PET image reconstruction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiplexed PET (mPET) using one tracer labeled with a positron plus prompt gamma ray emitter is limited by low sensitivity to triple-photon coincidences (two annihilation photons and one prompt gamma photon), leading to high noise in the reconstructed images. PURPOSE: The use of regularization has been previously shown to increase the image quality of single tracer PET images under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions. We will demonstrate the use of regularization in simultaneously acquired multi-tracer mPET data reconstruction. METHODS: First, we present how a maximum a posteriori expectation maximization solution can be obtained for simultaneously acquired multi-isotope PET data. Next, we use a Monte Carlo simulation of an image quality phantom mPET acquisition with a pure positron (18F) and a positron plus prompt gamma (44Sc) emitter to evaluate the performance of different regularization methods. RESULTS: For a baseline regularization method to simultaneously reconstruct both activity distributions, we show that a relative difference penalty (RDP) provides the best tradeoff of the penalty functions tested in image quality and quantitative accuracy for a simulated hot sphere phantom compared to quadratic and log-cosh penalty functions, with a contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in 18F/44Sc of over 60% higher on average for the RDP compared to the quadratic penalty in the largest spheres. However, this regularization approach has up to 2x worse reconstructed inter-tracer crosstalk ratio compared to unregularized reconstruction. Finally, we present a further optimization by alternating reconstruction of the two individual tracer images with regularization to achieve a CNR in the largest 18F/44Sc spheres with an up to 35% improvement on average over the simultaneous RDP-based regularization reconstruction results described above, while maintaining a 10%-20% lower inter-tracer crosstalk ratio over the unregularized reconstruction. CONCLUSIONS: For the selected radionuclides, simulated system and phantom, we demonstrate proof-of-principle that using regularization applied to an alternating update form of EM achieves significantly higher CNR in both tracers compared to unregularized alternating update OSEM and regularized simultaneous OSEM, with significantly lower crosstalk in the prompt gamma emitter reconstruction than the regularized simultaneous OSEM.

articles.title: Task-based detectability and angular-sampling bounds on spatial resolution in cone-beam micro-CT: a closed-form scan-design analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Spatial resolution in preclinical cone-beam micro-CT is conventionally characterised by image-domain metrics measured on a specific reconstruction of a specific phantom. Such metrics conflate resolution loss originating in the data (photon noise, angular undersampling) with resolution loss originating in the reconstruction (apodization, regularisation, voxel grid), and do not answer how much room is left for improvement on a given dataset. PURPOSE: To derive and evaluate two reconstruction-independent resolution limits for preclinical cone-beam micro-CT, a photon-noise limit from the projection-domain signal-known-exactly, background-known-exactly (SKE/BKE) ideal observer with the Rose criterion, and an angular-sampling limit from the Crowther criterion, and combine them into a single spatially varying picture that bounds what any classical reconstruction can achieve from a given scan. METHODS: We derived closed-form expressions for the photon-noise minimum detectable disc diameter and an off-axis fan-beam extension, and combined them with the Crowther criterion via pointwise minimum. All resolution limits are theoretical evaluations of these closed forms for the geometry of a representative preclinical micro-CT scanner. The only experimentally measured input is the unattenuated photon count per pixel, estimated from two flat-field projections, and the exposure and projection-count sweeps are hypothetical formula inputs, not acquired scans. The closed forms were validated by Poisson Monte Carlo simulation, and the specimen detectability map by fan-beam forward projection of a previously acquired mouse attenuation map. The optimum split of a fixed total photon budget was derived analytically. RESULTS: The combined limit yields a closed-form scan-design optimum. For the disc-detection task, the maximum worst-case spatial frequency scales as the cube root of the total photon budget per detector pixel (per-view flux times number of views), and an analytic rule sets how to split that budget between flux and views. The off-axis bound follows a "bowl" geometry rising from the centre to the rim, and the parametric sweeps show how each acquisition parameter reshapes this map. Simulated detectability agrees with the closed forms within 1% in minimum detectable diameter, on- and off-axis, and forward-projected real anatomy shifts the photon-noise limit by only + 3  to + 8 %  , confirming the uniform specimen model is conservative. CONCLUSIONS: The two reconstruction-independent limits combine into a usable engineering picture for scan design and detectability prediction in preclinical cone-beam micro-CT. The photon-noise limit is a task-based detectability threshold for a specified feature and contrast, expressed in frequency units rather than as a Fourier cutoff, and the combined map is a practical summary of these two independent, necessary constraints. Reconstructions that incorporate strong signal priors may exceed the Crowther limit at the cost of relying on those priors, but cannot exceed the photon-noise limit at any cost. An accompanying open-source interactive web calculator (https://ubc-ford-lab.github.io/ideal_observer_SKE_BKE_model/) implements these bounds for arbitrary scanner geometries.

articles.title: A generalizable 3D dose prediction across heterogeneous cohorts: A framework developed for the 2025 AAPM GDP-HMM challenge.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Manual radiotherapy treatment planning is labor-intensive, subjective, and highly variable across planners and institutions. Deep learning has emerged as a promising approach for estimating achievable three-dimensional (3D) dose distributions for a given plan (hereafter: dose prediction) by directly mapping patient anatomy and beam geometry to voxel-wise dose. However, achieving robust generalization across diverse anatomical sites, prescriptions, and institutions remains a major challenge, particularly under computational constraints required for clinical deployment. PURPOSE: We sought to develop and evaluate a generalizable, computationally efficient 3D dose prediction framework capable of spanning heterogeneous multi-site and multi-cohort datasets, as defined in the 2025 AAPM Generalizable Dose Prediction for Heterogeneous Multi-Cohort and Multi-Site (GDP-HMM) Grand Challenge. Our goal was to design a model that not only achieved state-of-the-art voxel-wise accuracy but also maintained clinically meaningful dose-volume and geometric characteristics across diverse cases. METHODS: We implemented a fully convolutional 3D dose-prediction model adapted from the MedNeXt architecture, which was originally introduced as a high-capacity convolutional backbone for medical image segmentation and is well suited to volumetric dense prediction tasks. The network accepted multimodal inputs comprising CT, PTV/OAR masks, beam and angle plates, and scalar plan metadata. A composite loss function combined voxel-wise L1, body-masked weighted L1, structure-wise moment-matching, and gradient-based penalties to jointly preserve spatial fidelity and dosimetric accuracy. The model was trained on the fixed GDP-HMM dataset consisting of 2876 training plans, 356 validation plans, and a held-out test set of 498 plans using random 3D patches and evaluated by mean absolute error (MAE), homogeneity index (HI), and conformity indices (CI100%, CI50%). Ablation studies quantified the contribution of each loss component to overall performance. Statistical comparisons used paired Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction. RESULTS: The proposed model achieved a mean voxel-wise MAE of 2.04 Gy on the validation set, outperforming the challenge baseline (2.54 Gy). An ensemble with the baseline further improved MAE to 1.94 Gy on the validation set and 2.071 Gy on the held-out test set, corresponding to the lowest test-set MAE and first-place overall ranking in the GDP-HMM Challenge. Predicted dose distributions preserved key plan characteristics, with ΔHI, ΔCI100%, and ΔCI50% narrowly centered around zero, indicating consistent target coverage and dose conformity. Protocol-specific evaluations for head-and-neck and lung cohorts demonstrated close alignment with reference plans, with no systematic degradation in OAR endpoints. Ablation experiments showed that removing gradient-based terms increased MAE by 0.50 Gy, while excluding the moment-matching term increased MAE by 0.06 Gy confirming that both gradient- and moment-based constraints enhanced spatial and dosimetric fidelity. CONCLUSION: We present a generalizable 3D dose prediction framework that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while satisfying stringent runtime requirements (< 3s per case on < 24 GB GPU memory). By integrating gradient-aware and moment-based constraints within a MedNeXt backbone, the model preserved clinical DVH endpoints and geometric plan features. These findings demonstrate that carefully engineered loss formulations are pivotal for cross-institutional generalization. The framework offers a foundation for rapid dose prediction that could accelerate treatment planning, reduce inter-planner variability, and enable intelligent automation in radiotherapy workflows.

articles.title: Can we assess brain perfusion on a regional basis from digital subtraction angiography images with motion artifacts?
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: A method called IPEN (for Intra-operative PErfusion assessment with No gantry rotation) has been developed that uses x-ray angiography images and assesses volumetric soft tissue perfusion on a regional basis. It has the potential to enable quantitative cross-sectional perfusion assessment before, during, and after interventional procedures, such that physicians can assess the risk and outcome of the procedure. However, the current IPEN will not function if there is no native (non-subtracted) x-ray angiography images available and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) images are corrupted by motion artifacts. PURPOSE: To demonstrate that region-based tissue enhancement can be extracted from DSA images even if they are contaminated by motion artifacts. METHODS: We developed a motion-compensating IPEN framework using DSA images (called MCI-D) and validated its core formulation. A key breakthrough enabling MCI-D was the finding that, even when DSA images contain motion artifacts, subtracting two DSA images can isolate the change in tissue enhancement between the images if motion is absent between the two times. RESULTS: A qualitative assessment using computer simulated XCAT perfusion phantom data validated the finding, and clinical data supported the feasibility. An extensive, systematic, and quantitative assessment showed that MCI-D was highly correlated to the ground truth (e.g., the correlation coefficients > 0.99 for both the time-enhancement curve and the blood flow perfusion index, maximum slope of the rising part of the time-enhancement curve). CONCLUSIONS: MCI-D enables accurate motion-compensated perfusion assessment from DSA images, even in the presence of severe motion artifacts, provided that the motion is not continuous and occurs within a short period of time.

articles.title: Low latency and generalizable dynamic MRI via L+S alternating gradient descent and minimization.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dynamic MRI reconstruction often requires accurate, fast, and low-latency algorithms that generalize across multiple applications, sampling schemes, and rates, without problem-specific parameter tuning. Existing methods either lack generalizability or require extensive parameter adjustment. PURPOSE: To develop generalizable, low-latency MRI reconstruction algorithms based on low-rank (LR) and low-rank + sparse (L+S) models that are accurate, fast, and require minimal parameter tuning across diverse dynamic MRI settings. METHODS: We propose a novel Alternating Gradient Descent and Minimization (AltGDmin) approach for L+S matrix recovery from column-wise undersampled measurements, and extend it to a 3-level hierarchical L+S model for dynamic MRI. A few-shot (FS) learning modification (AGM-L+S-FS) is introduced to enable near low-latency reconstruction with per-frame processing time comparable to or faster than scan time. A simpler LR-only variant is also evaluated. RESULTS: The proposed algorithms were validated on 6 prospective and 12 retrospective dynamic MRI datasets, covering cardiac, speech, and abdominal applications, with Cartesian, pseudo-radial, radial, and spiral sampling schemes. Experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction, generalizability across datasets and sampling rates, and low-latency performance. Detailed comparisons with state-of-the-art LR, L+S, low-latency, and unsupervised deep learning methods show superior or comparable performance. CONCLUSIONS: Our AGM-L+S-FS approach provide generalizable, fast, and low-latency MRI reconstruction across multiple dynamic MRI applications and sampling schemes, without the need for problem-specific parameter tuning.

articles.title: From Free Text to Research-Ready Data: A Reproducible, Reverse-Audited Pipeline for Structuring Breast Mammography Reports.
articles.abstract: Exported PDF mammography and pathology reports contain rich phenotypic and molecular information, yet they remain underused for research because converting them into research-ready variables is labor-intensive and error-prone. We developed a rule-based pipeline (PyMuPDF text extraction with section-aware regular expressions) that structured 615 source PDF reports into a verified 299 patient cohort (mean age 52.4 years; 290 female, sex not recorded in 9) with molecular subtype available for 286. An independent, deterministic reverse audit re-extracted every field from the source PDFs and compared it with the structured table across four validation layers, observing no discrepancies and confirming internal reproducibility rather than absolute accuracy. As a secondary, hypothesis-generating analysis, we used LASSO logistic regression under nested cross-validation (preprocessing and regularization tuned within training folds) to test whether report-level descriptors predict tumor biology. Predictive performance was weak throughout: HER2-positive versus HER2-negative attained the highest out-of-fold AUC 0.614 (95% CI 0.526-0.710), the only endpoint whose interval excluded chance, whereas triple-negative (0.511), four-class subtype (macro-AUC 0.519), and axillary node metastasis (0.455) were at or below chance. Incremental value benchmarks showed no gain over age or BI-RADS alone, and calibration and decision curve analysis indicated no clinically meaningful net benefit. These exploratory findings are consistent with evidence that pixel-level radiomics is more informative than report text; finer-grained NLP- or LLM-derived features remain unexplored. Under compatible report templates, the pipeline yields a reproducible, auditable structured breast cohort from text-exportable PDFs, motivating image-based radiomics as a reusable asset for multicenter research.

articles.title: Multi-Level Cancer Classification with FlexiFocusNet Using a Novel Nigerian Computed Tomography Imaging Dataset and Standard Histopathology Data.
articles.abstract: Reliable and generalisable artificial intelligence-based cancer image analysis remains challenging because of data scarcity, population bias, and the need to capture both local morphological details and long-range contextual dependencies. Many existing deep learning approaches rely on single-scale feature extraction or isolated attention mechanisms, potentially limiting their representation of multi-level spatial and channel information across imaging tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce FlexiFocusNet, an engineering-driven deep learning framework for multi-level cancer classification across heterogeneous medical imaging modalities. The architecture integrates hierarchical feature extraction, multi-scale attention fusion, transformer-style self-attention, and feature refinement to combine fine-grained local features with global contextual information. FlexiFocusNet was evaluated on a newly curated Nigerian computed tomography (CT) dataset for binary and three-class cancer classification and on a standard five-class histopathology dataset to examine its performance across imaging modalities. For binary CT classification, the model achieved 99.30 ± 0.49% accuracy, 99.62 ± 0.43% balanced accuracy, and an AUC of 1.000 under five-fold cross-validation, with 98.04% accuracy, 98.09% balanced accuracy, and an AUC of 0.999 on the independent test set. For three-class CT classification, it achieved 98.36 ± 1.05% validation accuracy and 98.01 ± 1.12% balanced accuracy, with 98.83% test accuracy, 98.52% balanced accuracy, and an AUC of 0.996. On five-class histopathology data, FlexiFocusNet achieved 99.92 ± 0.05% validation accuracy and 99.89 ± 0.06% balanced accuracy, followed by 100% test accuracy and an AUC of 1.000. The consistently high performance across the evaluated tasks indicates effective feature learning across different classification settings and imaging modalities. The study also contributes an underrepresented Nigerian CT dataset, subject to applicable institutional data-sharing requirements, providing an additional resource for research on cancer image analysis and geographically diverse medical artificial intelligence.

articles.title: UNICAL: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Learning with MRI-Derived Synthetic Amyloid PET for Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
articles.abstract: Limited availability of amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) motivates imaging-informatics methods that derive complementary molecular-imaging representations from routinely acquired magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We developed UNICAL, an uncertainty-aware multimodal framework for Alzheimer's disease-spectrum versus cognitively normal classification that combines a self-supervised three-dimensional MRI encoder, Contourlet Wavelet Stationary Radiomics (CoWS-Rad) engineered MRI features, and MRI-derived synthetic 18F-florbetapir (AV45) PET. CoCoLIT generated four stochastic PET realizations per MRI; their mean and voxelwise variance were used for uncertainty gating before probability-anchored transformer fusion. Synthetic PET was validated in 228 paired OASIS-3 MRI-AV45 examinations, achieving a mean per-examination voxelwise Pearson correlation of r = 0.864 and strong cortical-composite SUVR agreement with acquired PET (Pearson r = 0.954). In the OASIS-3 development cohort (813 sessions from 811 participants), participant-grouped five-fold cross-validation repeated across 20 seeds yielded AUROC 0.868 and expected calibration error (ECE) 0.061. The OASIS-3 development endpoint used the manuscript's AD-spectrum reference standard, whereas ADNI3 used AD-versus-CN research-group labels, providing cross-dataset evaluation on a related but non-identical prediction endpoint. Without retraining, feature refitting, threshold optimization, or recalibration, the frozen framework was evaluated in an independent matched ADNI3 cohort of 261 participants (87 AD, 174 CN), achieving AUROC 0.836 (95% CI 0.791-0.876). ECE increased to 0.089 under external transfer, indicating that calibration was more sensitive to domain shift than rank discrimination. Ablation analysis and K-sample sensitivity supported the contributions of uncertainty gating, adaptive weighting, modality dropout, residual correction, and the K = 4 synthesis configuration. UNICAL therefore provides an uncertainty-aware MRI-derived multimodal representation for AD-spectrum classification that retains substantial cross-dataset discrimination while remaining distinct from acquired molecular imaging and not replacing amyloid PET as a clinical biomarker.

articles.title: Improving Coronary Artery Stenosis Segmentation Performance of YOLO Models Through a Dataset Expansion Strategy Based on Local Focused Augmentation.
articles.abstract: To address the problems of the small size of coronary artery stenosis regions, strong background interference, and limited high-quality annotated data in X-ray coronary angiography images, a dataset expansion strategy based on local focused augmentation is proposed. The method uses existing annotations of stenotic regions to crop local images centered on the lesion regions and adds them to the original training set, thereby increasing the proportion of lesion regions in the training samples without requiring additional manual annotation. Experiments were conducted using the YOLOv8 and YOLO11 model series, and the applicability of the proposed method was evaluated under different learning rates and batch sizes. The results show that local focused augmentation improves the F1 score under most parameter settings. Further validation on the public ARCADE dataset showed that the precision, recall, and F1 scores of YOLOv8m-seg, YOLOv9c-seg, YOLOv11m-seg, and YOLO26m-seg were all improved, with the F1 score of YOLOv8m-seg increasing from 0.3868 to 0.4045. The proposed method can enhance the learning of local features of coronary artery stenosis and improve the segmentation performance of small stenotic regions without modifying the network architecture.

articles.title: Fast Multiparametric ASL MRI via Multi-Dimensional Acceleration and Subspace Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Multi-post-labeling delays (PLDs) multi-echo times (TEs) arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI enables simultaneous quantification of cerebral blood flow (CBF), arterial transit time (ATT), and blood-brain barrier (BBB) water exchange, but requires long scan times due to the combination of multi-TEs, PLDs, and repeated control-label acquisitions. A five-dimensional (5D) acquisition and reconstruction framework was developed to enable accelerated multi-parametric ASL. METHODS: A coordinated undersampling strategy was designed across in-plane k-space, through-plane k-space, TE, and control-label measurement dimensions, achieving a combined acceleration factor of approximately 28. Reconstruction was performed using a Kronecker-structured subspace model that exploited low-rank correlations along the TE and control-label dimensions. Sparsity regularization was applied in the subspace coefficient domain, and temporal bases were estimated from a single fully sampled middle slice. The framework was evaluated using in vivo echo-time-resolved ASL (TASL) datasets from eight subjects. RESULTS: The proposed reconstruction outperformed a matched compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction across all echo times, yielding higher structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), with the largest improvements observed under severe undersampling (R≈28) and at late echo times. Higher-fidelity CBF, ATT, BBB, and intravascular transit time (ITT) maps were obtained, with the greatest gains observed for BBB and ITT. Test-retest reliability, assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), remained comparable to fully sampled reference data. CONCLUSION: Coordinated multi-dimensional undersampling combined with Kronecker subspace reconstruction enables highly accelerated multi-parametric ASL while preserving image quality, quantitative parameter estimation, and test-retest reliability, supporting clinically feasible acquisition times.

articles.title: A Multicenter Ultrasound Habitat Radiomics Framework For Diagnosing Tuberculous Lymphadenitis And Stratifying Rifampicin Resistance Risk.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate an ultrasound-based habitat radiomics framework for the hierarchical differentiation of tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) from non-tuberculous lymphadenopathy, and to noninvasively predict rifampicin resistance risk using an independently collected cohort of patients with confirmed TBLN. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, 618 patients with superficial lymphadenopathy who underwent ultrasound examination between January 2022 and December 2025 at four tertiary hospitals were included. Among them, 530 patients with definitive diagnoses were used for diagnostic differentiation and were divided into a model-development (training) cohort and an external validation cohort, while 236 patients with confirmed tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) were included for rifampicin resistance risk assessment. Based on standardized B-mode ultrasound images, we developed a 2-stage ultrasound habitat radiomics framework that first differentiated tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes. Rifampicin resistance risk was assessed within the confirmed TBLN cohort using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA), and model interpretability was assessed using SHAP-based methods. RESULTS: For differentiating tuberculous from non-tuberculous lymph nodes, the habitat-based model demonstrated strong discriminative performance, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 in the training cohort and maintaining consistent performance in the external test cohort. Using nested cross-validated out-of-fold predictions within the confirmed TBLN cohort, the habitat-based model achieved an AUC of 0.83 for predicting rifampicin resistance, outperforming conventional radiomics and demonstrating superior clinical net benefit. Spatial visualization revealed that high-risk habitats were localized to specific intralesional regions, underscoring the importance of spatial heterogeneity in both disease diagnosis and drug resistance assessment. CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-based habitat radiomics provides an interpretable and clinically applicable framework for hierarchical diagnosis of tuberculous lymphadenitis and for rifampicin resistance risk assessment in an independent patient cohort, supporting precision imaging-guided management of tuberculosis.

articles.title: Development and Multicenter Validation of a Hybrid Radiomics-Deep Learning Model for Risk Stratification of O-RADS 4 Adnexal Masses.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-driven hybrid model integrating ultrasound radiomics, deep learning (DL) signatures, and clinical predictors for differentiating benign from borderline/malignant Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System (O-RADS) 4 adnexal masses, and to evaluate its utility as a radiologist decision-support tool. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter study retrospectively enrolled 653 patients from four centers (521 from Center A [training, n = 405; internal validation, n = 116]; 132 from Centers B-D [external validation]), and prospectively enrolled 126 patients from Center A. Pathological results served as the gold standard. Radiomics features were extracted to generate a Rad-score using machine learning classifiers. A transfer learning-based DL model using convolutional neural networks produced a DL-score. A hybrid model integrating Rad-score, DL-score, and clinical predictors was constructed. Diagnostic performance of models was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). In the prospective validation set, six radiologists interpreted cases with and without hybrid model assistance. Diagnostic differences were assessed using McNemar's χ² test, and inter-reader agreement by Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: The hybrid model demonstrated good performance with AUCs of 0.88 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.82-0.93) and 0.86 (95% CI: 0.78-0.92) in the prospective and external validation sets. Model assistance significantly improved accuracy and specificity across all readers (p < 0.05), with inter-reader agreement improving from kappa 0.49 to 0.73. The model stratified lesions into low-risk (4a) and high-risk (4b) subcategories with consistently distinct malignancy rates across all datasets (4a: 4.5%-16.1%; 4b: 75.4%-97.1%). CONCLUSION: The hybrid model demonstrated good performance for risk stratification of O-RADS 4 adnexal masses and improved radiologist performance across experience levels.

articles.title: Multimodal Photoacoustic/Ultrasound Imaging System for Longitudinal Assessment of Keloid Treatment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of using a multimodal photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging system for longitudinal monitoring of keloid lesions during intralesional therapy, and to assess its potential as an objective tool for treatment follow-up. METHODS: A patient with 5 keloids underwent serial imaging at 5 time points during intralesional injections of betamethasone and 5-fluorouracil. Clinical assessment was performed using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS). A multimodal photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging system which integrates different techniques was used to monitor structural, vascular, oxygenation, and elasticity changes during treatment. Structural parameters were assessed by grayscale ultrasound (GSUS), vascularity was evaluated by ultrasonographic microvascular angiography (UMA) and photoacoustic imaging (PAI), while oxygen saturation (SO2) provided by PAI, and elasticity was measured via elastography. RESULTS: VSS scores decreased significantly from 7.6 ± 2.3 at baseline to 2.2 ± 1.6 at T4 (p = .001), with improvements in pigmentation (p = .003), pliability (p = .009), and vascularity (p = .004). GSUS showed a reduction in total lesion thickness from 26.8 ± 10.5 mm to 8.0 ± 4.5 mm (p = .006), along with significant decreases in lesion lengths (p < .05). PAI demonstrated a decline in blood flow signals and an increase in SO2 levels in most lesions. UMA and PAI revealed reduced vascular density during treatment. Early-stage increases in stiffness were observed, but subsequent measurements became unfeasible as the lesions thinned. CONCLUSION: A multimodal PA/US imaging system provides comprehensive and noninvasive assessment of both structural and functional changes in keloids during treatment. This longitudinal study suggests its potential as a valuable tool for objective and dynamic monitoring of therapeutic response in scar management.

articles.title: Editorial for "Monitoring Remyelination and Its Association With Disability Improvement in Multiple Sclerosis Using APART-QSM MRI: A Longitudinal Cohort Study".
Doppler Ultrasonography and Computed Tomography Angiography in Carotid Artery Stenosis: Discordance and Its Potential Impact on Surgical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The degree of carotid artery stenosis influences surgical decision-making; therefore, accurate assessment is essential for appropriate patient selection. This study evaluated agreement between Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) in patients with significant stenosis detected on DUS and investigated factors associated with discordance. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 79 patients who underwent DUS between January 2024 and October 2025 were included. DUS stenosis grade, CTA stenosis according to NASCET and ECST methods, lumen diameters, plaque characteristics, and accompanying vascular features were evaluated. RESULTS: Agreement between DUS and CTA was fair using NASCET (κ = 0.413; p < .001) and moderate using ECST (κ = 0.531; p < .001). Agreement between NASCET and ECST was substantial (κ = 0.799; p < .001). Discordance was most frequent in the 50-69% DUS stenosis group and varied according to stenosis severity and CTA measurement method. Plaque type, plaque length, and calcification were not associated with discordance. Residual lumen diameter on CTA was significantly larger in NASCET-based discordant cases (p = .018) whereas no significant difference was observed using ECST classification. In some patients, discrepancies could potentially affect surgical decision-making. CONCLUSION: Agreement between DUS and CTA in significant carotid stenosis was fair using NASCET and moderate using ECST, with discordance particularly frequent in the 50-69% stenosis group and dependent on the CTA measurement method. Combined assessment with 2 noninvasive imaging modalities may help reduce misclassification in patients considered for surgical treatment.

articles.title: Joint a priori kinetic modeling with neural ODE for dual-tracer dynamic PET separation.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous dual-tracer dynamic PET imaging acquires a time series of images and could streamline oncology workflows by enabling the quantification of complementary biological processes in a single session. However, separating the superimposed tracer signals from the resulting mixed image sequence remains a key challenge. We introduce a physics-informed framework that combines Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (NODEs) with a priori compartmental kinetic models to achieve robust signal separation and generate individual tracer image sequences. By embedding the tracer dynamic models directly into the learning procedure, our method ensures the decomposed time-activity curves (TACs) are physically consistent. A superpixel-based preprocessing step clusters voxels in the dynamic data into homogeneous regions, substantially improving noise robustness and computational efficiency. Experiments on clinical dynamic PET data confirm our approach accurately reconstructs the individual tracer image sequences, outperforming existing methods. This work provides a generalizable solution for dual-tracer dynamic PET, with direct implications for the diagnosis of prostate tumors.

articles.title: Preoperative prediction of pathological grading in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: the incremental value of multiparametric spectral computed tomography.
articles.abstract: AIM: Preoperative assessment of the pathological grade of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is critical for determining therapeutic strategies, yet conventional imaging often lacks sensitivity. This study investigated the incremental value of multiparametric spectral computed tomography (CT) imaging in the noninvasive prediction of PDAC differentiation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 125 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC (77 poorly differentiated, 48 nonpoorly differentiated). All patients underwent triple-phase contrast-enhanced spectral CT. Quantitative parameters, including virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) at 40 to 140 keV, iodine concentration (IC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and the slope of the spectral curve (λHU), were measured. A multiparametric logistic regression model was developed to integrate these biomarkers, and a nomogram was constructed to visualise the predictive performance. RESULTS: Poorly differentiated tumours exhibited significantly lower values in 40 keV VMI, IC, Zeff, and λHU compared to nonpoorly differentiated tumours (P < .05). While individual spectral parameters showed moderate diagnostic ability, the exploratory three-phase combined model achieved the highest predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.75). For clinical application, a simplified venous-phase nomogram based on four independent predictors was constructed, yielding an AUC of 0.68 with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = .61). CONCLUSION: Spectral CT-derived quantitative parameters differ significantly between PDAC differentiation grades. A multiparametric approach integrating these parameters yields moderate discriminative performance (AUC 0.75) for preoperative grading-superior to single-parameter analysis but insufficient for stand-alone decision-making. Thus, it may serve as a complementary tool to assist risk stratification, requiring cautious interpretation alongside established clinical and pathological assessments.

articles.title: A decade of image-guided pleural biopsies: a multicentre retrospective study assessing diagnostic yield and complication rate.
articles.abstract: AIM: Pleural disease is common, with diagnostic options including pleural effusion cytology and pleural biopsy, either by local anaesthetic thoracoscopy (LAT) or image-guided biopsy. LAT facilitates multiregion sampling and simultaneous effusion management but may not be feasible with a loculated pleural space. Using long term local data, we assessed the diagnostic yield (DY) and complications associated with ultrasound-guided pleural biopsy (USGPB) and computed tomography-guided pleural biopsy (CTGPB). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicentre cohort study across 6 hospitals, retrieving data regarding USGPB and CTGPB performed in these hospitals between 01/01/13 and 31/03/23 using study code and key word searches. Patient demographics, pathology, final diagnosis (by biopsy or consensus diagnosis), and complications were recorded. RESULTS: A total of 194 CTGPBs were performed; 166/194 were diagnostic (DY 85.6%). 7/194 (3.6%) had a peri-procedural pneumothorax on CT, but none required intervention. For diagnosis of pleural malignancy, the sensitivity of CTGPB was 93.9% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 88.9%-97.0%), specificity 100% (89.1%-100%), positive predictive value (PPV) 100% (97.6-100%) and negative predictive value (NPV) 76.2 (63.7-85.4%). Ninty-three USGPBs were performed, all without post-procedural pneumothorax; 83/93 were diagnostic (DY: 89.2%). For pleural malignancy diagnosis, sensitivity of USGPB was 94.1% (95% CI: 84.5%-97.7%), specificity 100% (59.0%-100%), PPV 100% (94.6%-100%) and NPV 60.0% (37.5%-76.5%). CONCLUSION: CTGPB and USGPB are safe and accurate for diagnosis of pleural malignancy in cases where LAT is not available or feasible.

articles.title: Change in left atrioventricular coupling index from acute to chronic phases for prediction of major adverse cardiac events after myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: AIM: Previous studies confirmed the usability of the left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI) to enhance risk stratification of cardiovascular adverse events in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). We intend to study the prognostic value of the change in LACI (ΔLACI) from the acute to the chronic phases to predict major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in an AMI patient cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 264 patients following AMI were included in a secondary analysis. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed in the acute and chronic stages. LACI was defined by the ratio of left atrial to left ventricular end-diastolic volumes. MACE, including all-cause mortality, reinfarction, or heart failure after the follow-up examination (52 [interquartile range {IQR}: 47-61] months after AMI), was defined as the primary endpoint. RESULTS: Among the 264 participants (median age, 59 years [IQR 50-66]; 229 men), MACE occurred in 41 patients over 52 months after the first imaging. LACI was higher in patients with MACE (P< 0.001). The Youden Index identified a LACI cut-off at 24% and a ΔLACI cut-off at 0.02%/month (both P < 0.001) to classify high-risk patients. After adjusting for multivariate models, ΔLACI (model 1, hazard ratio [HR]: 0.46, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.36-0.60; model 2, HR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.50-0.78; both P < 0.001) was an independent predictor of MACE. ΔLACI enabled further risk stratification in AMI (LACI > 24%, P < 0.001; LACI < 24%, P = 0.013). CONCLUSION: LACI and ΔLACI provide superior prognostic value for MACE in AMI patients. ΔLACI provides incremental prognostic value beyond baseline LACI.
